prediction_ref.short_label: Enterprises self-host open-weight code models over hosted China APIs by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Unsloth tagged v0.1.47-beta on June 18 ("GLM 5.2 + Model Hub + 3x longer contexts"), and the build directly strengthens the run-the-open-weights-inside-your-own-boundary side of this prediction. It adds full GLM-5.2 support across all reasoning levels in Unsloth Studio - the same fully-open MIT coding family the prediction names as the data-sovereignty inflection - so teams can now not just serve but locally fine-tune those weights on hardware they control. The auto-fit context algorithm paired with multi-token prediction roughly triples usable context in fixed memory (a single 32GB f16 GPU rising from about 23,040 to 64,000 tokens without spilling), lowering the hardware bar that keeps self-hosting practical at scale, and the release restores vLLM 0.22+ compatibility plus a --secure Cloudflare-only encrypted-studio mode that speaks directly to the keep-the-inference-and-data-in-my-boundary posture. This is the local-stack-maturation that makes self-hosting permissively-licensed weights a real procurement alternative to routing code through a foreign-hosted API, and the week's confidential-computing thread keeps the same sovereignty concern live. It corroborates the trajectory rather than the named landing: no enterprise, regulated-sector buyer, or tooling framework has yet published guidance or a default that prefers self-hosting on data-jurisdiction grounds, and the context-fit figures are a beta's self-reported numbers.

prediction_ref.short_label: Inline MCP-channel policy enforcement ships as a platform default by Q1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Nous Research's Blank Slate setup mode for the open-source Hermes Agent framework (June 20) boots an agent with only a provider/model plus File-Operations and Terminal toolsets, while web, browser, code execution, vision, memory, delegation, cron, skills, plugins and MCP servers all stay off until explicitly enabled, written durably via platform_toolsets.cli and agent.disabled_toolsets so an update cannot silently re-enable them. The structurally relevant part for this prediction is that MCP access is gated default-off at the harness boundary before any tool invocation is allowed, the same move-the-control-point-into-the-runtime direction the prediction tracks - access decided where the agent runs rather than bolted on as a perimeter proxy. It is corroborating context for the broader pattern, not the named landing: Hermes enforces per-tool enablement at the application/harness layer, not the per-agent scoped MCP-channel network-layer enforcement the prediction specifically requires, and it is a fourth open framework's default rather than the third major agent platform or cloud runtime shipping documented inline MCP-channel policy distinct from Zscaler and Databricks.

prediction_ref.short_label: Agent meta-harness becomes the cross-vendor policy plane for agents by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Three agent-harness state-changes landed June 18-20 and together they push more autonomy and more control into the coding-agent layer the prediction watches. Nous Research's Hermes Blank Slate mode boots an agent least-privilege - only File-Operations and Terminal on, everything else durably gated off - a security posture applied at the harness level; OpenAI's Codex Record & Replay (macOS build 26.616) captures a desktop workflow once and re-runs it unattended; and Cisco open-sourced FAPO, a Claude-Code-driven pipeline-aware prompt optimizer that attributes failures to a stage and reports a +14.1-point mean gain over GEPA. This is the agent-governance-moving-up-into-the-harness direction the prediction names. But the match is contextual, not the landing: each is a single-vendor harness governing or optimizing its own agents, which the prediction explicitly excludes - none is a vendor-neutral meta-harness enforcing budgets, permissions or sandboxing uniformly across two or more rival agent runtimes, and no enterprise governance framework yet names the meta-harness tier as the prescribed policy-enforcement point.
